name: Van der Pol oscillator
description:
Van der Pol's oscillator, x'' − μ(1 − x²)·x' + x = 0, as two compartments: x, and y = dx/dt. The damping is negative for small swings and positive for large ones, so every start except the origin winds onto the same closed orbit, a limit cycle of amplitude 2.009 and period 6.663. At μ = 1 the problem is not stiff, and dp45 crosses the twenty seconds in 185 steps. Both states go negative, so "cannot go negative" is off on each.

Try: start x at 0.1 instead of 2 and watch the swing grow onto the same cycle. Raise mu and the cycle sharpens into slow drifts and sudden jumps; the next example is this model at μ = 1000, the standard stiff test problem.
